name: Art Deco watch
summary: The rectangular watch that Louis Cartier drew in 1917 after the plan of a tank seen from above. It has two side bars, a railway minute track, blued sword hands and a cabochon on the crown. The case is platinum or gold.

philosophy.core_thesis: A watch is a piece of jewellery with a plan. It has straight lines, black and white, and a rich metal, with no curve that has no job.
design_principles: Draw the case as a rectangle about 23 mm wide and 30 mm long, with two parallel side bars that run into the lugs.
Print Roman numerals inside a railway minute track that forms a rectangle.
Cut the hands as blued steel swords.
Set a cabochon of sapphire or ruby on the crown.
Use black, white and one precious metal; add colour with enamel or gems only.
Keep the face flat and the lines straight; round only the crown and the strap.
Mount diamonds in a platinum frame with milled edges, in straight rows of baguettes.
Fit a strap of black or brown crocodile with a gold or platinum buckle.
anti_patterns: A round pocket-watch case with a bow
A thick sporty case with a rotating bezel
The curved lines of art nouveau

silhouette.shape: A rectangle about 23 mm by 30 mm with two straight side bars that form the lugs, on a narrow strap.
silhouette.line: Straight and parallel lines; the only curve is the crown and the bend of the strap.
silhouette.fit: The case sits flat on the top of the wrist, and the strap curves round it.
silhouette.proportion: Case width to length is about 3 to 4. The dial fills about 75 per cent of the case. Strap width equals the width between the lugs.
rules: Make the side bars as long as the case and as wide as 3 mm.
Place the crown in the middle of the short side, at 3 o'clock.
Keep the numerals to 12 Roman numerals and draw the track as a rectangle.
Match the strap width to the lug gap, so that case and strap read as one line.

fabrics.rule: Use platinum or gold for the case, black or white enamel for the dial, and a crocodile strap; add stones only in straight rows.

methods: case cut and finished in gold or platinum
black enamel ring fired on the dial
railway minute track printed in black
construction.closures: A gold or platinum folding clasp, or a buckle, closes the strap; a cabochon crown winds and sets the watch.
construction.details: Sword hands of blued steel, a cabochon crown, Roman numerals and the side bars as lugs.

surface.pattern: A white or silver dial with a black railway track and Roman numerals; a black enamel ring for a cocktail model.
surface.gloss: Polished gold and platinum at 80 to 100 GU; black enamel at 90 to 100 GU; crocodile strap at 20 to 40 GU.
surface.wear: Platinum scratches and keeps its colour; gold shows rub marks at the side bars; crocodile skin creases and a strap is renewed after some years.

palette.strategy: Black and white with one metal; blue enters only in the hands and the crown stone.

processes: case cut in gold or platinum
making.scale: A jeweller's workshop made small series; the first model went on sale in 1919.
making.signs: Parallel side bars, a railway track, sword hands and a stone on the crown.

pieces.form: Rectangular case with two side bars as lugs

Black enamel ring dial with white Roman numerals

emotion.target_response: A cool urban elegance: the viewer sees straight lines, black and white and a rich metal.

modifiers.how: Cast the case in steel, add a bezel with eight screws and an integrated bracelet, and keep the clean dial.
Make the case round in steel, the dial black with large luminous numerals, and the strap canvas.
